problem: The sentence is corrupted: "let L = lim (aₙ/bₙ) with 0 1), Σaₙ converges." The condition on L and one whole direction of the conclusion have dropped out, so the test cannot be read. As printed it also fails to say that no conclusion is possible when L = 0 or L = ∞.
fix: Limit comparison: let bₙ > 0 and L = lim (aₙ/bₙ). If 0 < L < ∞, then Σaₙ and Σbₙ both converge or both diverge. If L = 0 and Σbₙ converges, then Σaₙ converges. If L = ∞ and Σbₙ diverges, then Σaₙ diverges.

problem: The rule reads "if L  1, it diverges". The case L < 1 (converges) has been lost, so the test as printed is incomplete and its inequality symbols are missing. A student copying this gets a wrong rule.
fix: Ratio test: if L < 1 the series converges absolutely; if L > 1 (including L = ∞) it diverges; if L = 1 the test gives no conclusion.

problem: The answer is corrupted: "The ratio (aₙ/bₙ) → 1, and 0 1), the series converges." The limit comparison condition and the reason Σ1/n² converges are both missing, so the argument does not hang together.
fix: Take bₙ = 1/n² > 0. Then aₙ/bₙ = (n+1)n²/(n³+2) = (n³+n²)/(n³+2) → 1, so L = 1 and 0 < L < ∞. Both series behave alike. Since Σ1/n² converges (p-series with p = 2 > 1), Σ (n+1)/(n³+2) converges.

problem: "The p-series is the real part of the Riemann zeta function" is false. For real s > 1, ζ(s) = Σ1/nˢ is exactly the p-series with p = s; it is not a real part of anything.
fix: The p-series with p = s is the Riemann zeta function ζ(s) = Σ1/nˢ for real s > 1.

where: Section 2, first step of the method list
problem: "Check f(x) = aₓ is positive..." mixes the index x with the term aₙ. The integral test was stated with aₙ = f(n), so the check should be written on f(x) alone, with aₙ read off as f(n).
fix: Check that f(x) is positive, continuous and decreasing for x ≥ 1, where aₙ = f(n).

problem: Σ1/(n log n) is given as an example the condensation test "handles", without saying the outcome. Many students will read this as an example that converges, but this series diverges.
fix: For example, Σ1/(n log n) gives Σ2ⁿ/(2ⁿ log 2ⁿ) = (1/log 2)Σ1/n, which diverges, so Σ1/(n log n) diverges; the test also settles Σ1/(n(log n)²), which converges.

problem: The placeholder text "[formula]" is left in front of the ratio limit, before "L = lim |aₙ₊₁/aₙ|".
fix: Delete the placeholder and keep only L = lim |aₙ₊₁/aₙ| with its definition list.
